newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate edges up 10 bps to 7.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate edges up 10 bps to 7.8 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate edged up 10 basis points to 7.8 percent on Monday in brisk interbank trade, the Zagreb Money Market reported.
Settlements totalled 37.6 million kuna and dealers put new borrowing at 21 million. Supply was 213 million kuna.
Interbank call money was steady at eight percent but the weighted rate rose to 8.3 from 7.7 percent after one loan from an insurance firm was rolled over at 11 percent.
Insurers' 31-366 day rate was also up to 12 from 11.5 percent. They granted short-term funds at a steady 7.0 percent.
The week-end overnight trade was livelier, totalling 112.8 million kuna as three banks with shortfalls squared positions.

Croatia's central bank said it stayed out of the foreign exchange market. Its kuna midrates for Tuesday's dealings were weaker at 5.2706 and 3.5538 to the dollar and the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
